title: Alert issued for very heavy rain in Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Keralam and Odisha - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange color warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall along with thunderstorms and lightning over Odisha and Rajasthan tomorrow. Alert has been issued for very heavy rain in Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi and Keralam. Northeast India including, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, and Karnataka will receive heavy rain tomorrow.

Meanwhile, the National Capital witnessed a consistent spell of rainfall in the past 24 hours.

title: Odisha Likely to Receive Heavy Rain From August 12 as Low-Pressure Area Over Bay of Bengal - prameyanews.com
article_text:
According to the IMD’s evening weather bulletin, the weather system is likely to trigger isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall across Odisha between August 12 and 14.
The IMD said an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas continues to persist. The circulation extends up to 7.6 km above mean sea level and tilts southwestwards with height.
Under its influence, a Low Pressure Area is likely to form over the same region around August 12.
Meanwhile, the Monsoon trough at mean sea level continues to run from Bikaner through Datia, the centre of the Low Pressure Area over north Madhya Pradesh and adjoining areas, Daltonganj and Digha before extending southeastwards into the east-central Bay of Bengal.
The trough extends up to 1.5 km above mean sea level, the weather office said.
The IMD has issued a yellow warning for heavy rainfall, which is very likely at one or two places in several districts of Odisha until August 18.
An orange warning has also been issued for heavy to very heavy rainfall at one or two places in the state onAugust 12, 13, 14 and 15.

title: Kalbaishakhi Storms Cause Heavy rainfall in Tripura, IMD Issues Warning - News On AIR
article_text:
A series of powerful Kalbaishakhi storms and heavy rainfall have caused widespread devastation across Tripura, paralyzing normal life in several districts. The Gomati district was among the hardest hit, with Udaipur, Amarpur, and Karbook sub-divisions reporting severed power lines and blocked national highways due to uprooted trees.

The Meteorological Department has issued a grim forecast, warning of continued heavy rain and gusty winds reaching up to 80 kilometres per hour over the next three days. Agartala witnessed severe urban flooding due to torrential rain.

title: IMD forecasts heavy to very heavy rainfall over Rajasthan & Odisha today - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Rajasthan and Odisha today.

According to IMD, thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty are expected to prevail over Lakshadweep, North Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today. The IMD has also predicted heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and lightning in various parts of the country over the next 2 to 3 days.

Akashvani correspondent reports that the Met Department predicted heavy rainfall along with thunderstorms and lightning over Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Rajasthan over the next two days.

Similar conditions are likely to prevail over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, and Sikkim. Meanwhile, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely to prevail over Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh till the 10th of this month.

Furthermore, Andhra Pradesh is expected to witness strong surface winds over the next three days. In Delhi NCR, the IMD has predicted light to moderate rainfall with a generally cloudy sky throughout the day.

title: देहरादून बारिश बढ़ाएगी मुश्किलें ! उत्तरकाशी में ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी, भारी बारिश के बीच फ्लैश फ्लड का खतरा - First India News
article_text:
देहरादून : बारिश मुश्किलें बढ़ाएगी. उत्तरकाशी में ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया गया है. उत्तरकाशी में भारी बारिश के बीच फ्लैश फ्लड का खतरा बढ़ गया है. यमुनोत्री, जखोल, हर्षिल, गंगनानी और नेलांग में फ्लैश फ्लड का खतरा है. उत्तरकाशी के संवेदनशील इलाकों में प्रशासन ने सतर्कता बढ़ाई है.
कुछ वॉटरशेड इलाकों में अचानक बाढ़ का कम से मध्यम खतरा है. भारी बारिश के बीच नदी-नालों के जलस्तर पर प्रशासन की नजर है. फ्लैश फ्लड के खतरे को देखते हुए संवेदनशील क्षेत्रों में अलर्ट जारी किया गया है. नदी-नालों के आसपास रहने वाले लोगों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी गई है. प्रशासन ने लोगों से सुरक्षित स्थानों पर रहने की अपील की  है. उत्तरकाशी में मौसम को देखते हुए प्रशासन पूरी तरह अलर्ट है.
आसमान से आफत, जमीन पर उफान :
चमोली की नीति घाटी में बादल फटने से भारी नुकसान की सूचना मिली है. तमक क्षेत्र में बादल फटने की सूचना से हड़कंप मच गया है. तेज बारिश के बाद तमक नाला उफान पर है, प्रशासन अलर्ट है. नीति घाटी में नुकसान का आकलन करने में प्रशासन जुटा है.
संवेदनशील इलाकों पर प्रशासन ने निगरानी बढ़ाई है. बादल फटने के बाद राहत-बचाव और सुरक्षा व्यवस्था को लेकर मोर्चा संभाला है. नीति घाटी में मौसम को देखते हुए प्रशासन पूरी तरह अलर्ट है. प्रशासन ने स्थानीय लोगों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी है.

title: J&K Weather Advisory: Heavy Rain, Flash Flood likely on August 11 - The Kashmir Horizon
article_text:
Monsoon spell intensifies as Srinagar hits 33.2°C ahead of forecasted downpours, landslides.

Srinagar: The Meteorological Centre in Srinagar has issued a severe weather advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, predicting widespread heavy to very heavy rainfall, particularly across the Jammu division, on Tuesday, August 11.

Forecasters warn that intense, short-duration spells could trigger flash floods, landslides, mudslides, and urban waterlogging in low-lying areas. Unsettled weather conditions marked by light to moderate rain are expected to persist through August 19. The advisory follows a warm 24-hour period where Srinagar recorded a maximum temperature of 33.2°C (3.2 degrees above normal) and Jammu settled at 34.6°C, while popular destinations Pahalgam and Gulmarg recorded highs of 27.2°C and 22.8°C, respectively. Disaster management authorities have urged residents and local administration in vulnerable zones to remain on high alert.
